r2_body: I beſeech thee, and doe mercifully with my maiſter Abra- ham. † Behold I ſtand nigh to the fountaine of water, and the daughters of the inhabiters of this citie, wil come forth to drawe water. † Therfore the maid, to whom I shal ſay: Bowe downe thy tankard that I may drinke : and she shal anſwere, Drinke, yea to thy camels alſo wil I geue drinke: she it is, whom thou haſt prouided for thy ſeruant Iſaac: and by this I ſhal vnderſtand, that thou haſt delt mercifully with my maiſter. † Neyther had he yet ended theſe wordes within him ſelfe, & behold Rebecca came forth, the daugh- ter of Bathuel, the ſonne of Melcha wife to Nachor the bro- ther of Abraham, hauinga tankard on her shoulder: † a paſ- ſing comely maide, & moſt beautiful virgin, & not knowen to man: and she was gone downe to the fountaine, and had filled her tankard, and came backe. † And the ſeruant ranne to mete her, and ſaid : Geue me a little water to drinke of thy tankard. † Who anſwered : Drinke my lord. And quickly she let downe the tankard vpon her arme, and gaue him drinke. † And when he had druncke, she added : but for thy camels alſo I wil drawe water, til al doe drinke. † And powring our the tankard into the troughes, she ranne backe to the wel to drawe water : and being drawen gaue it to al the camels. † But he muſing beheld her with ſilence, deſirous to know whether our Lord had made his iourney proſperous, or not. † And after that the camels had drunck, the man plucked forth golden carelettes, weying two ſicles: and as manie braceletts of tenne ſicles weight. † And he ſaid to her: whoſe daughter art thou? shew me : is there anie place in thy fathers houſe to lodge? † who anſwered: I am the daughter of Bathuel, the ſonne of Melcha, whom she bare ro Nachor. † And she added, ſaying: Of ſtrawe alſo and hay we haue good ſtore, and a large place to lodge in. † The man bowed him ſelfe, and adored our Lord, † ſaying : Bleſſed be the Lord God of my lord Abraham, rhat hath not taken away his mercie & truth from my lord, and hath brought me the ſtreight way into the houſe hauing pet- haps manie of my lords brother. † The maide therfore ranne, and re- wues and e- ported into ‖ her mothers houſe al things thatſhe had heard. uerie one a And Rebecca had a brother named Laban, who in al haiſt ſeueral houſs went forth to the man, where the fountaine was. † And ſhe went to her mother when he had ſeene the eareletts and braceletts in his ſiſters houſe.

lines.text: Abraham.
GENESIS.
I beſeech thee, and doe mercifully with my maiſter Abra-
ham. † Behold I ſtand nigh to the fountaine of water, and
the daughters of the inhabiters of this citie, wil come forth
to drawe water. † Therfore the maid, to whom I shal ſay:
Bowe downe thy tankard that I may drinke : and she shal
anſwere, Drinke, yea to thy camels alſo wil I geue drinke:
she it is, whom thou haſt prouided for thy ſeruant Iſaac:
and by this I ſhal vnderſtand, that thou haſt delt mercifully
with my maiſter. † Neyther had he yet ended theſe wordes
within him ſelfe, & behold Rebecca came forth, the daugh-
ter of Bathuel, the ſonne of Melcha wife to Nachor the bro-
ther of Abraham, hauinga tankard on her shoulder: † a paſ-

to man: and she was gone downe to the fountaine, and had
filled her tankard, and came backe. † And the ſeruant ranne
